keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the principle (a habit is a loop of a cue, a routine, and a reward) and the conclusion (understanding how habits work gives us more control than willpower alone). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why is simply trying harder often not enough to break a habit?
qs.qko: 왜 그냥 더 애쓰는 것만으로는 습관을 고치기 어려울까요?
opts: Because willpower gets tired, especially at the end of a long day
Because the cue disappears when we try harder
Because good habits always beat bad habits
evs: Willpower gets tired, especially at the end of a long day.
This saves mental energy, which is useful for good habits such as brushing your teeth.
Making a good habit very small and easy at first also helps, because small wins build the loop.
The cue is a trigger, such as a notification sound or the feeling of boredom.
why: 본문에 «Willpower gets tired, especially at the end of a long day» 라고 나와요. 의지력은 쉽게 지치기 때문에 더 애쓰는 것만으로는 부족해요.
The text says willpower gets tired, especially at the end of a long day, so trying harder is often not enough.

qs.q: In the text, what does the word "loop" mean?
opts: A cycle of cue, routine, and reward that repeats again and again
A rule that teachers give students about phones
A part of the brain that controls our feelings
evs: Many researchers describe a habit as a loop with three parts: a cue, a routine, and a reward.
The reward is the pleasant feeling that follows, which teaches the brain to repeat the loop next time.
A smarter approach is to change the loop itself.
The answer lies in habits, the actions we repeat so often that we barely think about them.
why: 습관을 신호·반복 행동·보상의 세 부분으로 된 고리라고 하고, 보상이 뇌에게 그 고리를 다음에도 반복하라고 가르친다고 해요. 계속 되풀이되는 순환이라는 뜻이에요.
A habit is a loop of a cue, a routine, and a reward, and the reward teaches the brain to repeat the loop. So a loop is a cycle that repeats.

qs.q: According to the text, how can you change a habit of scrolling on your phone?
qs.qko: 글에 따르면, 휴대폰을 계속 넘겨 보는 습관을 어떻게 바꿀 수 있나요?
opts: Remove the cue, or replace the routine with something better
Try harder and use more willpower late at night
Wait until the basal ganglia stops working
evs: For example, you can remove the cue by leaving your phone in another room while you study.
You can also keep the cue and the reward but replace the routine, such as stretching instead of scrolling when you feel bored.
Willpower gets tired, especially at the end of a long day.
Over time, a part of the brain called the basal ganglia takes over, so the action becomes almost automatic.
why: 휴대폰을 다른 방에 두어 신호를 없애거나, 지루할 때 스크롤 대신 스트레칭을 하는 식으로 반복 행동을 바꾸라고 해요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
You can remove the cue by leaving your phone in another room, or replace the routine, such as stretching instead of scrolling. You need both sentences.
